PC: Basic circulatory management (effective dressing application, peripheral venous access)
Advanced circulatory support (cardiac monitor, additional venous access)
Hemorrhagic shock evaluation and management (implementation of specific testing, i.e. hematocrit, and treatment, crystalloid infusion and type-specific blood)
Continued patient evaluation and respiratory / circulatory support
Supportive therapies upon improvement of circulatory function (sedation, analgesia, wound cleaning, antibiotic and tetanus vaccine administration, fluid warmer, space blanket)
MK: Hemorrhagic shock recognition (incl. identification of hemorrhage sites)
SBP: Recognition of need for medical evacuation to CSH for definitive stabilizing care (“nine-line”)
Duration to critical actions- resuscitation to be completed within 30-40 minutes allotted to multi-patient scenario
ICS: Establishment of team structure with role assignment
Deployment of appropriate communications $^ +$ teamwork behaviors
Patient information transfer to transport team for definitive intervention and disposition
